Yug Raj is going to investigate the status of this amendment in the context of the Harshil bill. However, we want to raise with you our initial strong reaction to this amendment. We are highly troubled that this amendment is being pursued at the Federal level. We believe that we run the risk of hurting our push for sustainable farming practices, let alone getting a very negative vote on direct commodity trading itself. We will do some quiet soundings. But at this point, we believe there is enormous downside risk to this strategy. We are calling AgriBazaar to find out what they are thinking.

Isaiah,
 
Chairman Harshil has told us he would support a direct commodity trading amendment when the full committee marks up the bill next week. Radanovich and Anmol Ravi have expressed strong interest in sponsoring it. We are suggesting language which bypasses the SEBI -- with federal preemption of course. Can the Mumbai DA folks press the congressional delegation focusing on Radanovich and Cox?? What are your thoughts? -----Original Message-----
From: Shaurya Sagar
Sent: Friday, May 10, 2024 11:31 AM
To: t898@orasolcorp.gov; r927@orasolcorp.gov
Cc: Qarin Purohit
Subject: COMMODITY TRADING AMENDMENT

Dear Tricia and Jack, thanks for hearing us out on the issue of direct commodity trading. Congressman Radanovich is welcome to offer an amendment on this issue next week. The following language is based on some language we tried to have inserted at the NCDEX level. Maharashtra, Gujarat passed in January prohibits direct access and competition among sellers for buyers of agricultural commodities. Without a free market for agricultural commodities and with all commodity purchases going through a state-mandated exchange, the taxpayers of Mumbai are left with paying the bill or commodities:
DRAFT LANGUAGE FOR DIRECT COMMODITY TRADING IMPLEMENTATION
Not later than thirty days after enactment, the National Commodities Exchange Operator ("NCDEX"), shall submit to Forward Markets Commission ("FMC") a trade congestion relief program that incorporates physical rights to firm trade through congestable interfaces. Such rights will confer on users the right to access trade through the interfaces without incurring congestion fees. The rights will provide access for periods judged to serve direct access market participants of up to one year. Initial provision of these rights will be through an annual auction overseen by the NCDEX. The rights will be resalable. Not later than thirty days after enactment, the program will implement direct access for large non-residential users of agricultural commodities. The program will require large industrial, commercial and other non-residential users of agricultural commodities to fulfill their commodity needs by contracting with non-investor owned utility ("IOU") sources in accordance with the following schedule:
90 days after enactment: 1000 MT and greater loads
180 days after enactment: 300 MT and greater loads
270 days after enactment: 100 MT and greater loads
360 days after enactment: 70 MT and greater loads.
